paramInfo.bow.dynamics: Bow speed and bow–bridge distance together, as players do it (mod wheel, CC 11). Velocity adds to it per note.
paramInfo.bow.pressure: Bow force relative to the playable window. Low: airy, surface sound. High: crunch and growl. Aftertouch adds to it.
paramInfo.bow.contact: Where the bow meets the string: over the fingerboard (dark, soft) to near the bridge (glassy). CC 74.
paramInfo.bow.bite: How hard notes start: higher means a faster bow acceleration and a stronger accent on loud notes.
paramInfo.bow.change: How quickly the bow reverses, on detached notes and when a long note runs out of bow. Slower is more audible.
paramInfo.bow.sustain: Below 1, held notes save bow: after the attack the bow slows (at the same contact point, as players do), so the note settles a little softer and the bow lasts longer between bow changes. 1 keeps the attack speed.
paramInfo.bow.auto: On: a long note changes bow when the bow runs out (every few seconds, as a player would). Off (the default): an endless bow, so long notes never break.
paramInfo.bow.legato: On: overlapping keys slur: the bow keeps going and the left hand changes the note. Within the hand's reach a finger lands or lifts (a quick, clean change); further away the hand shifts. Slur Range sets the widest interval that slurs. Off: every note changes bow.
paramInfo.body.coupling: How strongly the strings drive the bridge and body. It sets sympathetic ringing (open strings sound along with notes that match their harmonics) and how much the body loads the strings. 0: a rigid bridge.
paramInfo.chord.window: Keys pressed within this time of each other are one chord: two notes become a double stop on neighbouring strings, three or four are rolled.
paramInfo.chord.roll: How long the bow stays on each pair of strings when it rolls across a three- or four-note chord.
paramInfo.bow.friction: Thermal: rosin friction set by contact temperature (Woodhouse). Classic: a friction curve with hysteresis.
paramInfo.finger.intonation: How much the player corrects the pitch drop that heavy bowing causes on stopped notes. Open strings can't be corrected.
paramInfo.out.mode: Modelled: a synthetic body in stereo, calibrated to real recordings (CC0), with the controls beside it. Library Mic: the bridge force through a response measured from CC0 recordings (solo violin; for the cello, a cello section), with body, mics and room baked in. Pickup: the raw bridge force, like an electric instrument.
paramInfo.body.hill: The bridge's main resonance on the body (the 'bridge hill', around 2.6 kHz on a violin; the cello's sits lower, around 1.6 kHz, and moves with this control in proportion): lower is darker and warmer, higher is brighter. It moves the string's damping too, not just the tone.
paramInfo.body.wolf: A wolf eliminator (cello). On a cello the string and the body's strong resonance near 175 Hz (around F3 on the G and C strings) trade energy: the note beats, growls, and at light bowing won't speak at all. Real cellists clamp a small mass on a string behind the bridge to damp that resonance. 0: no eliminator, the wolf as the body makes it; 1: fully damped, the note even (and the body a little less resonant there).
paramInfo.body.mute: A mute on the bridge: its extra mass lowers and weakens the bridge hill, so the tone goes veiled and quieter in the highs.
paramInfo.body.resonance: The low body resonances' peaks and dips, which make some notes louder than their neighbours (around C#5-D5 especially). 1: as measured on a real violin. 0: smoothed out, for an even instrument. (Modelled output.)
paramInfo.out.width: The spacing of the stereo mic pair (Modelled output). At 1 the two mics are 60 cm apart, so each hears the violin from a slightly different direction and the treble differs between your ears, as in a real room. At 0 both are in one spot: mono.
paramInfo.bow.release: How a note ends when you let go. Lift: the bow leaves and the string rings on. Stop on String: the bow stops on the string and damps it, for a short, clean end. Finger Off: the bow leaves, then the finger, so the note falls to the open string. Auto: a quick key-up stops, a gentle one lifts (needs a keyboard that sends key-up speed).
paramInfo.finger.shift: How long a slurred shift slides, when a slurred note is out of the hand's reach (notes within reach are a quick finger change, with no slide). Bigger shifts slide longer, and key velocity sets the speed: a gentle key slides slowly and expressively, a hard one shifts quickly.
paramInfo.finger.noise: The whistle of the finger sliding over the string's winding during shifts (G, D and A strings; the steel E is plain).
paramInfo.string.select: Which string plays the notes, lowest to highest (violin G D A E, cello C G D A). Auto picks the usual string. A chosen string plays every note it reaches (up to two octaves above it): the lower strings give a darker, more intense sound.
paramInfo.string.keys: Keys C1 to E1 choose the string without sounding: C1 Auto, then C#1 to E1 the strings from lowest to highest (violin G D A E, cello C G D A).
paramInfo.instrument: Which instrument plays: Violin or Cello (viola and bass will be added here). Switching stops the notes that are playing. The cello is a first version: its strings are measured, but its bow, losses and body are still being calibrated against cello recordings.
paramInfo.artic: How new notes are bowed or played. Arco: ordinary bowing. Martelé: a bitten, accented stroke that stops on the string. Spiccato: off-the-string bounced notes. Tremolo: fast repeated bow strokes. Pizzicato: plucked. Harmonics: the finger touches the string lightly for a flute-like tone. Sautillé: a fast bouncing stroke, one note per bounce. Also on keys F1 to B1.
paramInfo.artic.tremRate: Bow strokes per second for Tremolo (each stroke is one direction). Players measure around 12 per second.
paramInfo.bow.velSens: How much key velocity changes each note's dynamics. At 0 every note follows the Dynamics knob; higher lets you shape phrases from the keys.
paramInfo.bow.atPressure: How much aftertouch (key pressure) adds bow pressure, for a growl or crunch on demand.
paramInfo.bow.noise: The bow hair's rosin noise: the slight hiss and grain of a real bow. 0 is a clean, synthetic string.
paramInfo.vib.depth: Vibrato width in cents (peak to peak) at a medium dynamic. Louder notes vibrate a little wider and faster, as players do. Open strings get none.
paramInfo.vib.rate: Vibrato speed. Players use about 5 to 7 Hz; it drifts a little from cycle to cycle.
paramInfo.vib.delay: How long a note sounds straight before the vibrato starts; it then fades in over about a third of a second. Recorded players vibrate from the start of the note, so the default is short (0.1 s).
paramInfo.room.mix: How much of the room you hear (with the Modelled output, at the default 1.5 m; further away there's more). The room hears the violin's sound in every direction, not just toward the mics, so it's darker and smoother than the direct sound. 100% in the Hall is about what a real hall gives at 1.5 m.
paramInfo.room.space: The kind of room: from a small room to a cathedral, or a plate reverb.
paramInfo.body.a0: The body's air resonance (the 'A0' mode: around 280 Hz on a violin, 100 Hz on a cello): the depth and warmth of the low strings. Its strength is the one measured trait that goes with violins players rate highly.
paramInfo.body.nasal: The region that sounds nasal and boxy when strong (0.8–1.5 kHz on a violin, lower on the cello): more gives the tone typical of factory instruments; less sounds sweeter and more open.
paramInfo.body.brilliance: The level of the bridge hill (around 2–3 kHz): presence and ring that carries in a hall. Bridge Hill sets its frequency.
paramInfo.body.softness: Cuts the top above about 4 kHz for a softer, rounder sound. Below 0 it adds air and edge.
paramInfo.body.voice: Moves all the body's resonances below 3 kHz up or down together, like a larger or smaller instrument: lower is darker and more alto-like, higher brighter and more soprano-like.
paramInfo.finger.style: How the player tunes. 0: equal temperament. Higher: as string players do, by ear from the open strings: leading tones a little high, notes that match an open string tuned to it, double stops pure.
paramInfo.vib.shape: How much the vibrato follows the music. 0: the same vibrato on every note. Higher: wider in high positions, narrower in fast passages (opening up on a held note), widening through long notes, a little faster on weak beats.
paramInfo.bow.metric: How much the player follows the meter when a host transport is playing: stronger beats a little louder, down-bows on strong beats and up-bows on pickups. 0 plays every note evenly. Off without a playing transport.
paramInfo.finger.portamento: Audible slides on slow, slurred leaps of a third or more, as in older or more romantic styles: above 0 the player keeps such leaps on one string and slides. 0 shifts cleanly and crosses strings instead; fast passages never slide.
paramInfo.finger.avoidOpen: Notes that would be open strings (D4, A4, E5) are played with the fourth finger on the string below when the playing isn't fast, so they can take vibrato, as players do. Off always uses the open string. Needs vibrato on; arco and martelé.
paramInfo.bow.slurRange: The widest interval that slurs. Overlapping keys further apart than this change bow instead, so only close notes are slurred. 24 slurs any leap.
paramInfo.mic.angle: Where the mics stand around the player (Modelled output). 0°: in front, facing the player; 90°: on the player's left, where the scroll points; −90°: on the right; 180°: behind. The violin's treble beams forward and up, so the sides are a little darker and behind is darker still. Every place has its own colour, changing from note to note.
paramInfo.mic.elevation: The mics' height, as an angle seen from the violin (Modelled output). 0°: level with it; 30° (default): a little above, the usual close-mic height; 90°: straight overhead. Below 0° the treble falls away: the violin radiates little toward the floor.
paramInfo.mic.distance: How far the mics are from the violin (Modelled output). Further away, the direct sound falls while the room stays, so you hear more room and a softer edge; the level is re-gained so it stays about as loud. 1.5 m is the default. Closer than 40 cm currently behaves like 40 cm (close-mic sound is coming).
paramInfo.bow.hairNoise: The bow's noise in a held note (cello): the hair's rasp between the harmonics, from about 100 Hz to 2 kHz, in a burst at every slip, measured from real cellos (the Iowa and bigcat recordings) as the part the friction alone doesn't make. Rosin Noise is the friction's own grain, higher up. 1: as the recordings; 0: none (the old, cleaner tone); 2: twice as much.
paramInfo.bow.catch: The bow's catch and scratch at the start of each stroke (cello), from a real cellist's recorded onsets (the Karoryfer x bigcat cello, CC0) with the note itself taken out, so the model still plays the note. 1: as the recordings, following each note as it builds up; 0: the model's attack alone; 2: twice as gritty. Bow changes get half, short strokes a short one, slurs, harmonics and pizzicato none.
paramInfo.bow.swell: How much a bowed note grows into its level, as players do. Real soft notes start gently and swell over about a fifth of a second; loud ones settle faster. 0: every note starts at full level at once (the old behaviour); 1: as the Philharmonia violinist plays. Slurred notes don't swell, and a new bow in a fast passage only a little.

body.wolf.why: The violin has no wolf note: choose the Cello.

bow.catch.why: Recorded onsets exist for the cello only so far: choose the Cello.

bow.hairNoise.why: Measured for the cello only so far: choose the Cello.
